Cardtly

01

The essence

Cardtly turns a business card into a living link you share with one tap. The brand should feel like the product: modern, effortless, and a little bit premium. Confident, never corporate.

In one line: the digital business card that does the work for you. It is tap-simple on the surface and quietly powerful underneath. The personality:

ModernEffortlessPremiumConfidentHumanConnected
02

Logo

Two marks. The badge is the primary identity for avatars, apps and icons. The wordmark is for headers and wide lockups. Both live on dark or neutral grounds where the gradient can glow.

Badge · primary

Wordmark · horizontal lockup

Clear space & minimum size

½C

Keep clear space of at least half the C-height on every side. Never crowd the mark with text or other logos.

Minimum size: 28px for the badge on screen, 10mm in print. Below that, detail in the 3D "C" is lost.

Do not

×Recolour the mark or drop the gradient
×Stretch, squash or rotate it
×Add shadows, outlines or extra glow
×Place it on a busy photo or a light clashing colour
×Rebuild the wordmark in another font
×Separate the "C" from the badge ring
03

Colour

The signature is the tri-tone gradient: cyan into violet into pink. Use it for the logo, key highlights and one hero moment per screen. Everything else stays on deep, near-black neutrals so the gradient does the talking.

Cardholders can accent their own card in eight colours (blue, purple, green, red, orange, pink, teal, gold). Those personalise a user's card. The three brand colours above are Cardtly's own and stay fixed.

04

Typography

Two typefaces, both free on Google Fonts. Syne carries the personality in headlines; Plus Jakarta Sans does the calm, legible work everywhere else.

Display · Syne

One tap.

Aa Bb Gg   0 1 2 3   & ? !

Headlines, the wordmark voice, big statements. Weights 700 and 800. Tight tracking. Use sparingly and large.

Body · Plus Jakarta Sans

Regular · the everyday reading weight
Medium · labels and emphasis
SemiBold · sub-headings
Bold · buttons and callouts

All body copy, UI, buttons and captions. Warm, humanist, highly legible on screens.

Type scale

Display / Syne 800Share it in one tap
Heading / Syne 700Everything a card should do
Body / Jakarta 400Your whole business card, shared with a tap.
Caption / Jakarta 500CARDTLY.COM/ANDRENEL
05

Voice & tone

Talk like a sharp, friendly professional, not a brochure. Short sentences. Say what the thing does. Confidence without hype.

Do

  • Lead with the benefit: "one tap and they've got you"
  • Use plain words a customer recognises
  • Be warm and human, a bit playful
  • Keep it short and active
  • Speak to South African businesses directly

Don't

  • Use jargon or "leverage / seamless / unlock"
  • Overpromise or shout in ALL CAPS
  • Sound like a corporate press release
  • Bury the point in a long sentence
  • Use em dashes anywhere, ever
House rule: Cardtly never uses em dashes in copy. Use a comma, a colon, or a full stop instead. It keeps the voice clean and consistent everywhere.
06

Imagery & feel

Dark, premium, and alive. Deep near-black grounds, soft gradient glow, glossy 3D surfaces, and always the real product: phones and cards caught mid-tap. Light backgrounds are fine for airy marketing moments, but the gradient is always the hero.
